newsitem.title: UK: Euro LSSR fuel strong but Russian HS fall away.
newsitem.headline: Euro LSSR fuel strong but Russian HS fall away.

text.p: Low sulphur straight-run fuel oil held firmly to strong levels on Tuesday but with no cargoes imminent business was at a standstill, traders said.
Russian high sulphur premiums were under pressure, with the sweep of buying that held prices up last week now ended.
"I think Russian values will come off sharply from now but there is no reason for the low sulphur not to hang around here for a while," said one trader.
Low sulphur was pegged at around $108/110 fob a tonne in NWE, a dollar up on the day, with one seller rumoured to be asking $111 for second decade August material.
An M100 straight-run was traded on Tuesday at around two means plus $3.50, traders reported, a sharp fall from deals last week done at around two means plus $6.

E4s were also drifing off, with refiners turning away from running residuary fuel in favour of crude. An E4 was heard done on Monday at three means plus $5, with Tuesday's value pegged at around $4 above the means.
